ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between hope and action in Shia theology according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the 'people of hope' (Ahl al-Amal) who rely on divine mercy while persisting in sin, declaring them false allies because their hope is merely wishful thinking. He establishes the principle that genuine hope is inextricably linked to action, paralleling how fear naturally drives one to flee from danger, thereby emphasizing the necessity of balancing hope with practical obedience.

en.hubeali: And it is reported by Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A group of people from the ones in your<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah are commiting minor sins of disobedience and are saying, ‘We (live in hope)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! There are no friends for us<sup>asws</sup> (like) those people. The belief is swaying with them. The one who hopes for something would work for it, and the one who fears from something, would flee from it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad has also narrated the above Hadith in a mafu’ manner from who has said the following: “

I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Certain people of your supporters commit smaller sins and say that they have hope (in Allah’s forgiveness).’ The Imam said, ‘They lie. They are not our supporters. They are a people whose hope has caused them to deviate. Whoever has hope in something, he works to achieve it. Whoever is afraid of something, he keeps away from it.’”
